# autom9 - Epic Breakdown

## Overview

This document provides the complete epic and story breakdown for autom9, decomposing the requirements from the PRD and Architecture into implementable stories.

## Requirements Inventory

### Functional Requirements

FR1: Consultant can view their open days and scheduled engagements sourced from Snowflake via the Tableau data source within the extension panel
FR2: Consultant can view their task list ingested from their designated individual Google Doc
FR3: Consultant can interact with the AI agent via a chat interface embedded in the Tableau extension panel
FR4: Agent can ask clarifying questions about task timing, priority, and scheduling preferences before taking action
FR5: Agent retains context within a session to support multi-turn clarifying conversations
FR6: Consultant can review the agent's proposed actions before execution is confirmed
FR7: Agent surfaces open work opportunities from the org-wide Google Doc, distinguishing billable client work from internal projects
FR8: Agent prioritises billable opportunities above internal project opportunities
FR9: Agent calculates whether a consultant's available capacity meets the time commitment of an open work opportunity, including a 5% buffer
FR10: Consultant can accept or decline an open work opportunity from within the extension panel
FR11: Agent notifies the relevant coordinator when a consultant accepts an open work opportunity
FR12: Agent does not resurface a previously declined opportunity to the same consultant
FR13: Agent submits a Smartsheet planning request on behalf of the consultant
FR14: Agent creates Google Calendar invites for the consultant around existing engagements
FR15: Extension checks connectivity to all configured integrations on load and surfaces any unavailable services before interaction begins
FR16: Agent fails gracefully with a specific error message if an integration becomes unavailable during a workflow, without partially executing dependent actions
FR17: Agent masks identifiable data fields (names, client identifiers, engagement IDs) with opaque tokens before transmitting any context to the LLM provider
FR18: Agent rehydrates masked tokens with real values from the session token map before displaying output or executing tool actions
FR19: Integration credentials are never exposed in logs, the chat interface, or configuration files visible to consultants
FR20: Admin can install and register the extension in Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server
FR21: Admin can configure the BYOM LLM provider and API credentials at the org level via the extension configuration panel
FR22: Admin can load and update the JSON workflow configuration file defining agent capabilities, tool access, and workflow parameters
FR23: Admin can test integration connections from the configuration panel before activating the extension for consultants
FR24: Admin can access agent interaction logs with sufficient detail to diagnose failed tool calls, error patterns, and latency
FR25: Integration status check results are logged for admin review
FR26: New agent workflows can be added by updating the JSON workflow configuration file without modifying platform code
FR27: The JSON workflow configuration defines available tools, agent instructions, and workflow parameters in a versionable format
FR28: The extension supports OpenAI and Anthropic as BYOM LLM providers, switchable via configuration change
FR29: The extension is compatible with Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server

### NonFunctional Requirements

NFR1: Agent responses complete within 20 seconds (p95) under normal operating conditions during the POC phase (nice-to-have; no hard SLA in v1)
NFR2: The extension panel renders and integration status check completes within 5 seconds of Tableau dashboard load
NFR3: The chat interface displays a visible processing indicator within 1 second of the consultant submitting a message
NFR4: All data transmitted between the extension and external services is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+)
NFR5: API credentials and integration tokens are stored encrypted at rest and never surfaced in logs, UI elements, or configuration files accessible to consultants
NFR6: The token masking system transmits no real consultant names, client identifiers, or engagement IDs to any external LLM provider under any circumstances
NFR7: Agent interaction logs capture only masked data representations — no raw LLM payloads containing identifiable fields
NFR8: The extension identifies and reports unavailability of any configured integration within the 5-second load status check window
NFR9: A failure in one integration does not cascade to prevent other integrations from functioning
NFR10: The JSON workflow configuration system handles version mismatches gracefully — a config update does not break or corrupt an in-flight session
NFR11: The extension supports concurrent usage by all 80 POC consultants without degradation in agent response time
NFR12: The platform architecture imposes no design constraints that would prevent future multi-tenant isolation

### Additional Requirements

- **[ARC-1] Project Scaffolding (Day-Zero):** Backend scaffold: `uv init autom9-backend` with fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy[asyncio], asyncpg, alembic, pydantic-settings, python-jose, httpx, cryptography, python-json-logger. Frontend scaffold: `npm create vite@latest autom9-extension -- --template svelte-ts` with @tableau/extensions-api-types.
- **[ARC-2] .trex Manifest:** Create `autom9.trex` at extension project root with required fields: name, description, source-location (backend URL), min-version, permissions (read worksheets). Without this the extension cannot load for any testing.
- **[ARC-3] CORS Configuration:** Configure FastAPI `CORSMiddleware` in `main.py` with allowed Tableau origins (public.tableau.com and Tableau Server domain).
- **[ARC-4] JSON Workflow Config Schema:** Document schema in `app/config/workflow_schema.py` — minimum fields: version (semver), tools (array with name, description, parameters), agent_instructions (string), workflow_id (string).
- **[ARC-5] Tableau initializeAsync Gate:** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` must complete before any store setup or backend calls in `App.svelte`.
- **[ARC-6] Alembic Fail-Fast:** Container must fail to start if migration fails. Enforced via Docker entrypoint exit code check.
- **[ARC-7] Async Test Setup:** `pytest.ini` must specify `asyncio_mode = auto`. Async SQLAlchemy fixtures must be function-scoped to prevent state leakage.
- **[ARC-8] Connection Pool Sizing:** `DATABASE_POOL_MIN` and `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` as environment variables (recommended: min=5, max=20) via pydantic-settings.
- **[ARC-9] masking.py Quality Gate:** `app/agent/masking.py` requires 100% branch coverage as a hard acceptance criterion for any story touching the agent pipeline.
- **[ARC-10] LLM Retry/Backoff Strategy:** `LLMProvider.complete()` must apply exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries max, then raise `ProviderError` on 429 or transient errors.
- **[ARC-11] Data Models:** Four core models required: `DeclinedOpportunity` (consultant_id, opportunity_id, declined_at), `InteractionLog` (session_id, masked_input, masked_output, tool_calls, latency_ms, timestamp), `CredentialStore` (org_id, provider, encrypted_key), `WorkflowConfig` (version, config_json, loaded_at), `Session` (session_id UUID PK, tableau_user_id, started_at).
- **[ARC-12] BYOM Provider Interface:** `LLMProvider` class with `complete()` and `stream()` — stream() raises `NotImplementedError` in v1.
- **[ARC-13] Integration Interface:** All integrations in `app/integrations/` implement `IntegrationBase` with `health_check()` and `execute()`. Failure raises `IntegrationError` caught at `app/api/` level.
- **[ARC-14] Session Registry:** `GET /api/admin/sessions/{session_id}` endpoint for admin triage. All `InteractionLog` entries reference session_id. PII stays out of logs.

### UX Design Requirements

No UX design document present for this project.

### FR Coverage Map

FR1:  Epic 3 — Tableau/Snowflake data panel
FR2:  Epic 3 — Individual Google Docs task list ingestion
FR3:  Epic 3 — Chat interface in extension panel
FR4:  Epic 3 — Agent clarifying Q&A before action
FR5:  Epic 3 — Multi-turn session context retention
FR6:  Epic 3 — Action confirmation before execution
FR7:  Epic 4 — Org-wide Google Doc open work surfacing
FR8:  Epic 4 — Billable > internal prioritisation
FR9:  Epic 4 — Capacity + 5% buffer calculation
FR10: Epic 4 — Accept/decline flow in panel
FR11: Epic 4 — Coordinator notification on accept
FR12: Epic 4 — Declined opportunity persistence
FR13: Epic 3 — Smartsheet planning request
FR14: Epic 3 — Google Calendar invite creation
FR15: Epic 1 — Integration health check on load
FR16: Epic 1 — Graceful failure isolation (pattern); Epic 3 (agent pipeline enforcement)
FR17: Epic 3 — Token masking before LLM calls
FR18: Epic 3 — Token rehydration before output/actions
FR19: Epic 2 — Credentials never in logs/UI/config
FR20: Epic 2 — Extension install (Desktop + Cloud)
FR21: Epic 2 — BYOM credential configuration (org-level)
FR22: Epic 2 — JSON workflow config load/update
FR23: Epic 2 — Integration connection testing from admin panel
FR24: Epic 2 — Admin interaction log access
FR25: Epic 2 — Status check results logged
FR26: Epic 2 — New workflows via JSON config, no code changes
FR27: Epic 2 — JSON config defines tools, instructions, params (versionable)
FR28: Epic 2 — OpenAI + Anthropic BYOM switching via config
FR29: Epic 1 — Tableau Desktop + Cloud/Server compatibility

## Epic List

### Epic 1: Platform Foundation & Extension Shell

The extension loads in Tableau, renders a status panel, and confirms that all configured integrations are reachable — giving consultants and admins a trustworthy starting point for every session.

**FRs covered:** FR15, FR16 (isolation pattern established), FR29
**ARCs covered:** ARC-1, ARC-2, ARC-3, ARC-5, ARC-6, ARC-7, ARC-8, ARC-11 (Session, CredentialStore, WorkflowConfig, InteractionLog only), ARC-12 (interface only), ARC-13 (interface only), ARC-14
**NFRs covered:** NFR2, NFR4, NFR8, NFR9, NFR12

> Note: `DeclinedOpportunity` model deferred to Epic 4 (migration-first — no schema for features not yet built).

### Epic 2: Admin Configuration & Extension Management

An admin can fully configure the extension — set BYOM credentials, load a JSON workflow config, test all integrations, and review interaction logs — making the extension ready for consultants to use.

**FRs covered:** FR19, FR20, FR21, FR22, FR23, FR24, FR25, FR26, FR27, FR28
**ARCs covered:** ARC-4, ARC-9 (quality gate policy defined), ARC-10 (LLM retry/backoff), ARC-12 (concrete OpenAI + Anthropic implementations), ARC-13 (concrete integration implementations)
**NFRs covered:** NFR5, NFR10

### Epic 3: Consultant Planning Request Workflow (Core POC)

A consultant can open the extension, see their open days and task list, have a multi-turn clarifying conversation with the agent, and complete a Smartsheet planning request with Google Calendar invites — without leaving Tableau.

**FRs covered:** FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4, FR5, FR6, FR13, FR14, FR16 (enforced in pipeline), FR17, FR18
**ARCs covered:** ARC-9 (masking.py 100% branch coverage gate enforced here)
**NFRs covered:** NFR1, NFR3, NFR6, NFR7, NFR11

### Epic 4: Open Work Discovery & Acceptance _(POC Stretch Goal)_

A consultant can browse open work opportunities (billable prioritised above internal), check their capacity against the commitment, accept or decline — with coordinator notification on acceptance and declined opportunities never resurfacing.

**FRs covered:** FR7, FR8, FR9, FR10, FR11, FR12
**ARCs covered:** ARC-11 (DeclinedOpportunity model + migration introduced here)
**NFRs covered:** NFR11 (capacity check logic)

**And** the plaintext key is never written to logs, response bodies, or any database column (FR19, NFR5)

**Given** credentials are stored
**When** the admin revisits the config panel
**Then** the key field displays a masked placeholder (e.g., `••••••••`) — the raw value is never returned by any API endpoint (NFR5)

**Given** invalid or missing credentials are submitted
**When** `POST /api/admin/credentials` is called
**Then** the API returns a `400` with a structured error — no stack trace or internal detail exposed

**Dev notes:** FR19, FR20, FR21, NFR5 — `AdminConfig.svelte` shell established here; other admin sections built in subsequent stories

---

### Story 2.2: JSON Workflow Configuration System

As an **admin**,
I want to upload and update a JSON workflow configuration file that defines the agent's available tools and instructions,
So that new agent workflows can be added or changed without modifying platform code.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a valid JSON workflow config is uploaded via `POST /api/admin/config`
**When** `WorkflowRegistry` processes the file
**Then** `validate_schema()` confirms the presence of required fields: `version` (semver), `workflow_id`, `tools` (array with `name`, `description`, `parameters`), `agent_instructions` (string)
**And** the config is stored in `workflow_configs` with `version`, `config_json`, and `loaded_at`

**Given** the extension loads
**When** `GET /api/config/workflow` is called
**Then** the current active workflow config is returned and `WorkflowRegistry.get_tool_definitions()` reflects the loaded tools (FR22, FR27)

**Given** a new config is uploaded while a session is in progress
**When** the in-flight session makes a subsequent tool call
**Then** the session continues using the config version it started with — no disruption or corruption (NFR10)

**Given** an invalid or version-mismatched config is uploaded
**When** `validate_schema()` runs
**Then** the upload is rejected with a clear error and the previous active config remains unchanged (FR26, FR27)

**Dev notes:** ARC-4, NFR10 — `WorkflowRegistry` class with `register_workflow()`, `get_tool_definitions()`, `validate_schema()`; file-backed in v1

---

### Story 2.3: BYOM Provider Implementations

As an **admin**,
I want to switch the active LLM provider between OpenAI and Anthropic via configuration,
So that the platform is not locked to a single model vendor.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** OpenAI is set as the active BYOM provider in credentials
**When** the agent makes an LLM call
**Then** `OpenAIProvider.complete()` is invoked with the correct message format for the OpenAI API

**Given** Anthropic is set as the active BYOM provider
**When** the agent makes an LLM call
**Then** `AnthropicProvider.complete()` is invoked with the correct Anthropic message format
**And** tool call formats are normalised behind the `LLMProvider` interface — the orchestration layer is unaware of provider differences (FR28)

**Given** the provider returns a `429` or transient error
**When** `LLMProvider.complete()` handles the response
**Then** exponential backoff with jitter is applied, retrying up to 3 times before raising `ProviderError` (ARC-10)

**Given** `LLMProvider.stream()` is called
**When** the method executes
**Then** it raises `NotImplementedError` (streaming deferred to v2; interface is set)

**Given** the provider is switched from OpenAI to Anthropic via a config change
**When** the next agent call is made
**Then** the new provider is used without requiring an app restart (FR28)

**Dev notes:** ARC-10, ARC-12 (concrete implementations), FR28

---

### Story 2.4: Integration Connection Testing

As an **admin**,
I want to test each integration connection from the config panel before activating the extension for consultants,
So that I can diagnose credential or connectivity issues before they affect consultant workflows.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the admin opens the config panel
**When** they click "Test Connections"
**Then** `POST /api/integrations/{name}/test` is called for each configured integration (Snowflake, Google Docs, Smartsheet, Google Calendar, LLM provider)
**And** results are displayed per integration with a pass/fail indicator and specific error message on failure (FR23)

**Given** an integration test call is made
**When** the integration's `health_check()` runs
**Then** it uses the concrete `IntegrationBase` implementation for that service
**And** failure raises `IntegrationError` — never propagates as an unhandled exception to the client

**Given** one integration test fails
**When** results are returned
**Then** the other integration test results are unaffected and still displayed (NFR9)

**Given** a test succeeds
**When** results are logged
**Then** the log entry contains `session_id`, integration name, and latency — no credential values (FR19)

**Dev notes:** ARC-13 (concrete IntegrationBase implementations for all 5 integrations), FR23

---

### Story 2.5: Admin Interaction Log Access

As an **admin**,
I want to retrieve masked agent interaction logs and resolve a session ID to a consultant identity,
So that I can diagnose failed tool calls, error patterns, and latency issues.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** agent interactions have occurred
**When** `GET /api/admin/logs` is called with optional filters (session_id, time range)
**Then** log entries are returned containing: `session_id`, `tool`, `latency_ms`, `masked_input`, `masked_output`, `timestamp`
**And** no entry contains consultant names, client identifiers, engagement IDs, or raw API keys (FR24, NFR7)

**Given** an admin needs to identify which consultant a session belongs to
**When** `GET /api/admin/sessions/{session_id}` is called
**Then** the `tableau_user_id` for that session is returned (ARC-14)
**And** this endpoint is restricted to admin-authenticated requests only

**Given** integration status checks have run
**When** `GET /api/admin/logs` is queried
**Then** status check results are included in the log output (FR25)

**Given** a log entry is written anywhere in the system
**When** the masking filter processes it
**Then** it passes through `app/agent/masking.py`'s masking pipeline before write — no raw PII ever reaches log storage (NFR7)

- Primary keys: `id` (UUID, `uuid4` default)

**API endpoints:**
- Plural nouns, kebab-case segments: `/api/integrations`, `/api/admin/logs`
- Path params: `{name}` FastAPI style — `/api/integrations/{name}/execute`
- Query params: `snake_case` — `?session_id=...`
- Custom headers: `X-Autom9-*` prefix — `X-Autom9-Token`

**Python (backend):**
- Modules/files: `snake_case` — `workflow_registry.py`, `masking.py`
- Classes: `PascalCase` — `WorkflowRegistry`, `LLMProvider`
- Functions/variables: `snake_case` — `get_tool_definitions()`, `session_id`
- Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` — `MAX_RETRIES`, `TOKEN_PREFIX`
- Pydantic schemas: suffix `Request`/`Response` — `ChatRequest`, `ChatResponse`

**Svelte/TypeScript (frontend):**
- Component files: `PascalCase.svelte` — `ChatPanel.svelte`, `StatusBar.svelte`
- Store files: `camelCase.ts` — `chat.ts`, `session.ts`
- TypeScript interfaces: `PascalCase` — `Message`, `IntegrationStatus`
- Variables/functions: `camelCase` — `sessionToken`, `sendMessage()`
- CSS classes: `kebab-case` — `.chat-panel`, `.status-bar`

### Format Patterns

**API response envelope — success:**
```json
{ "data": { ... }, "meta": { "request_id": "uuid" } }
```

**API response envelope — error:**
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "Smartsheet is currently unavailable",
    "integration": "smartsheet"
  }
}
```

- `code`: machine-readable `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` — used by extension to display specific messages
- Never expose stack traces or raw exceptions to the extension
- HTTP status codes: `200` (success), `400` (bad request), `401` (auth), `422` (validation), `503` (integration unavailable)
- Date/time: ISO 8601 strings everywhere — `"2026-04-08T14:30:00Z"`. Never Unix timestamps in JSON.
- JSON field names: `snake_case` throughout API. Frontend converts at `api.ts` boundary; internal Svelte state may use `camelCase`.

### Structure Patterns

**Backend tests:** `tests/` at project root mirroring `app/` — `tests/agent/test_masking.py` mirrors `app/agent/masking.py`.

**Test naming:** `test_{function}_{scenario}` — `test_mask_tokens_replaces_names`.

**Integration interface** — all integrations in `app/integrations/` implement:
```python
class IntegrationBase:
    async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus: ...
    async def execute(self, action: str, params: dict) -> dict: ...
```
Failure raises `IntegrationError` — caught at `app/api/` level, never propagates unhandled.

**BYOM provider interface:**
```python
class LLMProvider:
    async def complete(self, messages: list, tools: list) -> LLMResponse: ...
    async def stream(self, messages: list, tools: list) -> AsyncIterator[str]: ...
    # stream() raises NotImplementedError in v1; interface set for future streaming
```

**Masking pattern:** All data entering `app/agent/` is masked before LLM calls. All data leaving `app/agent/` toward response serialisation is rehydrated. Applied in `app/agent/masking.py` as a pipeline step — never inline in orchestration logic.

### Session Registry Pattern

Logs contain only opaque `session_id` — no consultant names or identifiers. Admin triage path: error in log → `session_id` → session registry → `tableau_user_id` → consultant identity.

**`Session` data model** (added to `app/models/`):
```
Session (session_id UUID PK, tableau_user_id TEXT, started_at TIMESTAMP)
```

**Admin endpoint:** `GET /api/admin/sessions/{session_id}` — returns `tableau_user_id` for a given session. Admin-only.

Session created on extension initialisation (before first chat message). All `InteractionLog` entries reference `session_id`. PII stays out of logs; session registry is a separate protected lookup table.

### State Management Patterns (Svelte)

**Store update pattern:** Always `update()` with new object — no direct mutation:
```typescript
chatStore.update(state => ({ ...state, messages: [...state.messages, newMsg] }))
```

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import AsyncIterator


@dataclass
class LLMResponse:
    content: str
    tool_calls: list[dict]
    finish_reason: str


class LLMProvider(ABC):
    """
    BYOM provider interface. All providers implement complete().
    stream() raises NotImplementedError in v1 — interface set for future streaming.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    async def complete(self, messages: list[dict], tools: list[dict]) -> LLMResponse:
        """
        Send messages to the LLM and return a complete response.
        Applies exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries max, on 429 or transient errors.
        Raises ProviderError after exhausting retries.
        """
        ...

    async def stream(self, messages: list[dict], tools: list[dict]) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        """Streaming not implemented in v1."""
        raise NotImplementedError("Streaming not supported in v1")
        if False:  # satisfy type checker
            yield ""

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.agent.anthropic_provider import AnthropicProvider
from app.agent.openai_provider import OpenAIProvider
from app.agent.provider import LLMProvider
from app.core.exceptions import ProviderError
from app.models.credential_store import CredentialStore
from app.services.encryption import decrypt

_ORG_ID = "default"

_PROVIDER_MAP: dict[str, type[LLMProvider]] = {
    "openai": OpenAIProvider,
    "anthropic": AnthropicProvider,
}


async def get_provider(db: AsyncSession) -> LLMProvider:
    """
    Resolve the active LLM provider from DB credentials.
    Queries DB on every call — supports provider switching without app restart (FR28).
    Raises ProviderError if no active credential exists.
    """
    result = await db.execute(
        select(CredentialStore).where(
            CredentialStore.org_id == _ORG_ID,
            CredentialStore.is_active.is_(True),
        )
    )
    row = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if row is None:
        raise ProviderError(
            "none",
            "No active LLM provider configured. Set credentials via admin panel.",
        )

    provider_cls = _PROVIDER_MAP.get(row.provider)
    if provider_cls is None:
        raise ProviderError(row.provider, f"Unknown provider '{row.provider}'")

    api_key = decrypt(row.encrypted_key)
    return provider_cls(api_key=api_key)

10	_ANTHROPIC_VERSION = "2023-06-01"
11	_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
12	_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 4096
13	_MAX_RETRIES = 3
14	_TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529}
15	
16	
17	class _ProviderHTTPError(Exception):
18	    def __init__(self, status_code: int, body: str) -> None:
19	        self.status_code = status_code
20	        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status_code}: {body}")
21	
22	
23	def _is_transient(exc: Exception) -> bool:
24	    if isinstance(exc, httpx.TimeoutException):
25	        return True
26	    if isinstance(exc, httpx.TransportError):
27	        return True
28	    if isinstance(exc, _ProviderHTTPError) and exc.status_code in _TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES:
29	        return True
30	    return False
31	
32	
33	def _backoff_wait(attempt: int) -> float:
34	    """Exponential backoff with full jitter: [0, 2^attempt) seconds."""
35	    return random.uniform(0, 2 ** attempt)
36	
37	
38	def _split_system_messages(messages: list[dict]) -> tuple[str | None, list[dict]]:
39	    """
40	    Extract system-role messages into a top-level system string.
41	    Anthropic does NOT accept {"role": "system", ...} in the messages array.
42	    """
43	    system_parts = []
44	    non_system = []
45	    for m in messages:
46	        if m.get("role") == "system":
47	            system_parts.append(m.get("content", ""))
48	        else:
49	            non_system.append(m)
50	    system = "\n".join(system_parts) if system_parts else None
51	    return system, non_system
52	
53	
54	def _tools_to_anthropic(tools: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
55	    """
56	    Convert internal tool definitions to Anthropic tool format.
57	    Internal format uses 'parameters'; Anthropic requires 'input_schema'.
58	    """
59	    return [
60	        {
61	            "name": t["name"],
62	            "description": t.get("description", ""),
63	            "input_schema": t.get("parameters", {"type": "object", "properties": {}}),
64	        }
65	        for t in tools
66	    ]
67	
68	
69	def _parse_content(content: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:
70	    """
71	    Parse Anthropic response content blocks into (text, tool_calls).
72	    Tool call 'input' is already a dict — no JSON parsing needed.
73	    Normalizes to internal format: {id, name, arguments: dict}.
74	    """
75	    text_parts = []
76	    tool_calls = []
77	    for block in content:
78	        if block.get("type") == "text":
79	            text_parts.append(block.get("text", ""))
80	        elif block.get("type") == "tool_use":
81	            tool_calls.append({
82	                "id": block.get("id", ""),
83	                "name": block.get("name", ""),
84	                "arguments": block.get("input", {}),
85	            })
86	    return "\n".join(text_parts), tool_calls
87

89	def _normalize_finish_reason(stop_reason: str | None) -> str:
90	    mapping = {
91	        "end_turn": "stop",
92	        "tool_use": "tool_calls",
93	        "max_tokens": "length",
94	        "stop_sequence": "stop",
95	    }
96	    return mapping.get(stop_reason or "", stop_reason or "stop")

99	class AnthropicProvider(LLMProvider):
100	    """Concrete LLMProvider implementation for the Anthropic Messages API."""
101	
102	    def __init__(
103	        self,
104	        api_key: str,
105	        model: str = _DEFAULT_MODEL,
106	        max_tokens: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
107	    ) -> None:
108	        self._api_key = api_key
109	        self._model = model
110	        self._max_tokens = max_tokens
111	
112	    async def complete(self, messages: list[dict], tools: list[dict]) -> LLMResponse:
113	        """
114	        Call Anthropic Messages API.
115	        Retries on transient errors with exponential backoff + jitter (ARC-10).
116	        Raises ProviderError after 3 retries.
117	        """
118	        system, filtered_messages = _split_system_messages(messages)
119	
120	        payload: dict = {
121	            "model": self._model,
122	            "max_tokens": self._max_tokens,
123	            "messages": filtered_messages,
124	        }
125	        if system:
126	            payload["system"] = system
127	        if tools:
128	            payload["tools"] = _tools_to_anthropic(tools)
129	
130	        last_exc: Exception | None = None
131	        for attempt in range(_MAX_RETRIES + 1):
132	            try:
133	                return await self._call_api(payload)
134	            except Exception as exc:
135	                if not _is_transient(exc):
136	                    raise ProviderError("anthropic", str(exc)) from exc
137	                last_exc = exc
138	                if attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
139	                    await asyncio.sleep(_backoff_wait(attempt))
140	
141	        raise ProviderError("anthropic", f"Max retries exceeded: {last_exc}") from last_exc
142	
143	    async def _call_api(self, payload: dict) -> LLMResponse:
144	        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
145	            response = await client.post(
146	                _ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES_URL,
147	                headers={
148	                    "x-api-key": self._api_key,
149	                    "anthropic-version": _ANTHROPIC_VERSION,
150	                    "content-type": "application/json",
151	                },
152	                json=payload,
153	            )
154	        if response.status_code != 200:
155	            raise _ProviderHTTPError(response.status_code, response.text)
156	        data = response.json()
157	        text, tool_calls = _parse_content(data.get("content", []))
158	        return LLMResponse(
159	            content=text,
160	            tool_calls=tool_calls,
161	            finish_reason=_normalize_finish_reason(data.get("stop_reason")),
162	        )

import logging
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import AsyncGenerator

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pythonjsonlogger.json import JsonFormatter

from app.api import integrations as integrations_router
from app.api import sessions as sessions_router
from app.api import status as status_router
from app.api.admin.config import router as admin_config_router
from app.api.admin.credentials import router as admin_credentials_router
from app.api.admin.logs import router as admin_logs_router
from app.api.config import router as workflow_config_router
from app.api.data import router as data_router
from app.config.workflow_registry import workflow_registry
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.exceptions import IntegrationError
from app.db.engine import AsyncSessionFactory


def _configure_logging() -> None:
    handler = logging.StreamHandler()
    handler.setFormatter(JsonFormatter())
    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.setLevel(settings.LOG_LEVEL)
    root.addHandler(handler)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
    _configure_logging()
    async with AsyncSessionFactory() as db:
        await workflow_registry.load_from_db(db)
    yield


app = FastAPI(title="autom9", lifespan=lifespan)

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=[o.strip() for o in settings.CORS_ORIGINS.split(",") if o.strip()],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

app.include_router(sessions_router.router)
app.include_router(status_router.router)
app.include_router(integrations_router.router)
app.include_router(admin_credentials_router)
app.include_router(admin_config_router)
app.include_router(admin_logs_router)
app.include_router(workflow_config_router)
app.include_router(data_router)


@app.exception_handler(HTTPException)
async def http_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: HTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    message = exc.detail if isinstance(exc.detail, str) else str(exc.detail)
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code,
        content={"error": {"code": str(exc.status_code), "message": message}},
    )


@app.exception_handler(IntegrationError)
async def integration_error_handler(request: Request, exc: IntegrationError) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=503,
        content={"error": {"code": "INTEGRATION_ERROR", "message": str(exc), "integration": exc.integration}},
    )


@app.get("/health")
async def health() -> dict:
    return {"status": "ok"}


@app.get("/api/health")
async def api_health() -> dict:
    return {"status": "ok"}

import logging
import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.db.deps import get_db
from app.models.session import Session as UserSession
from app.schemas.sessions import SessionCreateRequest, SessionCreateResponse

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/sessions", tags=["sessions"])


@router.post("", response_model=SessionCreateResponse, status_code=201)
async def create_session(
    body: SessionCreateRequest,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> SessionCreateResponse:
    session = UserSession(tableau_user_id=body.tableau_user_id)
    db.add(session)
    await db.flush()  # populate session.session_id before logging

    logger.info(
        "session_created",
        extra={"session_id": str(session.session_id)},
        # NOTE: tableau_user_id is NOT logged — it is PII
    )

    return SessionCreateResponse(
        data={"session_id": session.session_id, "started_at": session.started_at},
        meta={"request_id": str(uuid.uuid4())},
    )

import json

from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.config.workflow_schema import WorkflowConfigSchema
from app.models.workflow_config import WorkflowConfig


class WorkflowRegistry:
    """In-memory singleton holding the active workflow config.

    Lifecycle:
    - Populated from DB at app startup via load_from_db().
    - Updated atomically on each successful register_workflow() call.
    - Thread-safe for single-process async use (no concurrent writes from multiple
      Uvicorn workers in v1).
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._active: dict | None = None

    def validate_schema(self, config: dict) -> WorkflowConfigSchema:
        """Parse and validate config dict. Raises ValidationError on failure."""
        return WorkflowConfigSchema.model_validate(config)

    async def register_workflow(self, config: dict, db: AsyncSession) -> WorkflowConfig:
        """Validate, persist to DB as active, and update in-memory state.

        All previous rows are deactivated atomically before the new row is inserted.
        Raises pydantic.ValidationError if config is invalid — in-memory state is NOT
        updated, leaving the previous active config intact (NFR10 rollback safety).
        """
        parsed = self.validate_schema(config)  # raises ValidationError before any DB write

        # Deactivate all existing active configs
        await db.execute(update(WorkflowConfig).values(is_active=False))

        row = WorkflowConfig(
            version=parsed.version,
            config_json=json.dumps(config),
            is_active=True,
        )
        db.add(row)
        await db.flush()  # get row.id without committing; get_db dep commits at request end

        # Update in-memory state AFTER flush — only reaches here if DB write succeeded
        self._active = config
        return row

    def get_tool_definitions(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return the tools list from the active config.

        Returns [] if no config is loaded (fresh deployment, no config uploaded yet).
        """
        if self._active is None:
            return []
        parsed = WorkflowConfigSchema.model_validate(self._active)
        return [t.model_dump() for t in parsed.tools]

    @property
    def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        """Raw dict of the current active config, or None if none loaded."""
        return self._active

    async def load_from_db(self, db: AsyncSession) -> None:
        """Load active config from DB. Called once at app startup."""
        result = await db.execute(
            select(WorkflowConfig).where(WorkflowConfig.is_active.is_(True)).limit(1)
        )
        row = result.scalar_one_or_none()
        if row is not None:
            self._active = json.loads(row.config_json)


# Module-level singleton — imported by routers and lifespan
workflow_registry = WorkflowRegistry()

# 🎯 Story Context Quality Competition Prompt

## **🔥 CRITICAL MISSION: Outperform and Fix the Original Create-Story LLM**

You are an independent quality validator in a **FRESH CONTEXT**. Your mission is to **thoroughly review** a story file that was generated by the create-story workflow and **systematically identify any mistakes, omissions, or disasters** that the original LLM missed.

**Your purpose is NOT just to validate - it's to FIX and PREVENT LLM developer mistakes, omissions, or disasters!**

### **🚨 CRITICAL MISTAKES TO PREVENT:**

- **Reinventing wheels** - Creating duplicate functionality instead of reusing existing
- **Wrong libraries** - Using incorrect frameworks, versions, or dependencies
- **Wrong file locations** - Violating project structure and organization
- **Breaking regressions** - Implementing changes that break existing functionality
- **Ignoring UX** - Not following user experience design requirements
- **Vague implementations** - Creating unclear, ambiguous implementations
- **Lying about completion** - Implementing incorrectly or incompletely
- **Not learning from past work** - Ignoring previous story learnings and patterns

### **🚨 EXHAUSTIVE ANALYSIS REQUIRED:**

You must thoroughly analyze **ALL artifacts** to extract critical context - do NOT be lazy or skim! This is the most important quality control function in the entire development process!

### **🔬 UTILIZE SUBPROCESSES AND SUBAGENTS:**

Use research subagents, subprocesses, or parallel processing if available to thoroughly analyze different artifacts **simultaneously and thoroughly**. Leave no stone unturned!

### **🎯 COMPETITIVE EXCELLENCE:**

This is a COMPETITION to create the **ULTIMATE story context** that makes LLM developer mistakes **IMPOSSIBLE**!

## **🚀 HOW TO USE THIS CHECKLIST**

### **When Running from Create-Story Workflow:**

- The workflow framework will automatically:
  - Load this checklist file
  - Load the newly created story file (`{story_file_path}`)
  - Load workflow variables from `./workflow.md`
  - Execute the validation process

### **When Running in Fresh Context:**

- User should provide the story file path being reviewed
- Load the story file directly
- Load the corresponding workflow.md for variable context
- Proceed with systematic analysis

### **Required Inputs:**

- **Story file**: The story file to review and improve
- **Workflow variables**: From workflow.md (implementation_artifacts, epics_file, etc.)
- **Source documents**: Epics, architecture, etc. (discovered or provided)
- **Validation framework**: The workflow's checklist execution system

---

## **🔬 SYSTEMATIC RE-ANALYSIS APPROACH**

You will systematically re-do the entire story creation process, but with a critical eye for what the original LLM might have missed:

### **Step 1: Load and Understand the Target**

1. **Load the workflow configuration**: `./workflow.md` for variable inclusion
2. **Load the story file**: `{story_file_path}` (provided by user or discovered)
3. **Extract metadata**: epic_num, story_num, story_key, story_title from story file
4. **Resolve all workflow variables**: implementation_artifacts, epics_file, architecture_file, etc.
5. **Understand current status**: What story implementation guidance is currently provided?

**Note:** If running in fresh context, user should provide the story file path being reviewed. If running from create-story workflow, the validation framework will automatically discover the checklist and story file.

### **Step 2: Exhaustive Source Document Analysis**

**🔥 CRITICAL: Treat this like YOU are creating the story from scratch to PREVENT DISASTERS!**
**Discover everything the original LLM missed that could cause developer mistakes, omissions, or disasters!**

#### **2.1 Epics and Stories Analysis**

- Load `{epics_file}` (or sharded equivalents)
- Extract **COMPLETE Epic {{epic_num}} context**:
  - Epic objectives and business value
  - ALL stories in this epic (for cross-story context)
  - Our specific story's requirements, acceptance criteria
  - Technical requirements and constraints
  - Cross-story dependencies and prerequisites

#### **2.2 Architecture Deep-Dive**

- Load `{architecture_file}` (single or sharded)
- **Systematically scan for ANYTHING relevant to this story:**
  - Technical stack with versions (languages, frameworks, libraries)
  - Code structure and organization patterns
  - API design patterns and contracts
  - Database schemas and relationships
  - Security requirements and patterns
  - Performance requirements and optimization strategies
  - Testing standards and frameworks
  - Deployment and environment patterns
  - Integration patterns and external services

#### **2.3 Previous Story Intelligence (if applicable)**

- If `story_num > 1`, load the previous story file
- Extract **actionable intelligence**:
  - Dev notes and learnings
  - Review feedback and corrections needed
  - Files created/modified and their patterns
  - Testing approaches that worked/didn't work
  - Problems encountered and solutions found
  - Code patterns and conventions established

#### **2.4 Git History Analysis (if available)**

- Analyze recent commits for patterns:
  - Files created/modified in previous work
  - Code patterns and conventions used
  - Library dependencies added/changed
  - Architecture decisions implemented
  - Testing approaches used

#### **2.5 Latest Technical Research**

- Identify any libraries/frameworks mentioned
- Research latest versions and critical information:
  - Breaking changes or security updates
  - Performance improvements or deprecations
  - Best practices for current versions

### **Step 3: Disaster Prevention Gap Analysis**

**🚨 CRITICAL: Identify every mistake the original LLM missed that could cause DISASTERS!**

#### **3.1 Reinvention Prevention Gaps**

- **Wheel reinvention:** Areas where developer might create duplicate functionality
- **Code reuse opportunities** not identified that could prevent redundant work
- **Existing solutions** not mentioned that developer should extend instead of replace

#### **3.2 Technical Specification DISASTERS**

- **Wrong libraries/frameworks:** Missing version requirements that could cause compatibility issues
- **API contract violations:** Missing endpoint specifications that could break integrations
- **Database schema conflicts:** Missing requirements that could corrupt data
- **Security vulnerabilities:** Missing security requirements that could expose the system
- **Performance disasters:** Missing requirements that could cause system failures

#### **3.3 File Structure DISASTERS**

- **Wrong file locations:** Missing organization requirements that could break build processes
- **Coding standard violations:** Missing conventions that could create inconsistent codebase
- **Integration pattern breaks:** Missing data flow requirements that could cause system failures
- **Deployment failures:** Missing environment requirements that could prevent deployment

#### **3.4 Regression DISASTERS**

- **Breaking changes:** Missing requirements that could break existing functionality
- **Test failures:** Missing test requirements that could allow bugs to reach production
- **UX violations:** Missing user experience requirements that could ruin the product
- **Learning failures:** Missing previous story context that could repeat same mistakes

#### **3.5 Implementation DISASTERS**

- **Vague implementations:** Missing details that could lead to incorrect or incomplete work
- **Completion lies:** Missing acceptance criteria that could allow fake implementations
- **Scope creep:** Missing boundaries that could cause unnecessary work
- **Quality failures:** Missing quality requirements that could deliver broken features

### **Step 4: LLM-Dev-Agent Optimization Analysis**

**CRITICAL STEP: Optimize story context for LLM developer agent consumption**

**Analyze current story for LLM optimization issues:**

- **Verbosity problems:** Excessive detail that wastes tokens without adding value
- **Ambiguity issues:** Vague instructions that could lead to multiple interpretations
- **Context overload:** Too much information not directly relevant to implementation
- **Missing critical signals:** Key requirements buried in verbose text
- **Poor structure:** Information not organized for efficient LLM processing

**Apply LLM Optimization Principles:**

- **Clarity over verbosity:** Be precise and direct, eliminate fluff
- **Actionable instructions:** Every sentence should guide implementation
- **Scannable structure:** Use clear headings, bullet points, and emphasis
- **Token efficiency:** Pack maximum information into minimum text
- **Unambiguous language:** Clear requirements with no room for interpretation

### **Step 5: Improvement Recommendations**

**For each gap identified, provide specific, actionable improvements:**

#### **5.1 Critical Misses (Must Fix)**

- Missing essential technical requirements
- Missing previous story context that could cause errors
- Missing anti-pattern prevention that could lead to duplicate code
- Missing security or performance requirements

#### **5.2 Enhancement Opportunities (Should Add)**

- Additional architectural guidance that would help developer
- More detailed technical specifications
- Better code reuse opportunities
- Enhanced testing guidance

#### **5.3 Optimization Suggestions (Nice to Have)**

- Performance optimization hints
- Additional context for complex scenarios
- Enhanced debugging or development tips

#### **5.4 LLM Optimization Improvements**

- Token-efficient phrasing of existing content
- Clearer structure for LLM processing
- More actionable and direct instructions
- Reduced verbosity while maintaining completeness

---

## **🎯 COMPETITION SUCCESS METRICS**

**You WIN against the original LLM if you identify:**

### **Category 1: Critical Misses (Blockers)**

- Essential technical requirements the developer needs but aren't provided
- Previous story learnings that would prevent errors if ignored
- Anti-pattern prevention that would prevent code duplication
- Security or performance requirements that must be followed

### **Category 2: Enhancement Opportunities**

- Architecture guidance that would significantly help implementation
- Technical specifications that would prevent wrong approaches
- Code reuse opportunities the developer should know about
- Testing guidance that would improve quality

### **Category 3: Optimization Insights**

- Performance or efficiency improvements
- Development workflow optimizations
- Additional context for complex scenarios

---

## **📋 INTERACTIVE IMPROVEMENT PROCESS**

After completing your systematic analysis, present your findings to the user interactively:

### **Step 5: Present Improvement Suggestions**

```
🎯 **STORY CONTEXT QUALITY REVIEW COMPLETE**

**Story:** {{story_key}} - {{story_title}}

I found {{critical_count}} critical issues, {{enhancement_count}} enhancements, and {{optimization_count}} optimizations.

## **🚨 CRITICAL ISSUES (Must Fix)**

{{list each critical issue with clear, actionable description}}

## **⚡ ENHANCEMENT OPPORTUNITIES (Should Add)**

{{list each enhancement with clear benefit description}}

## **✨ OPTIMIZATIONS (Nice to Have)**

{{list each optimization with benefit description}}

## **🤖 LLM OPTIMIZATION (Token Efficiency & Clarity)**

{{list each LLM optimization that will improve dev agent performance:
- Reduce verbosity while maintaining completeness
- Improve structure for better LLM processing
- Make instructions more actionable and direct
- Enhance clarity and reduce ambiguity}}
```

### **Step 6: Interactive User Selection**

After presenting the suggestions, ask the user:

```
**IMPROVEMENT OPTIONS:**

Which improvements would you like me to apply to the story?

**Select from the numbered list above, or choose:**
- **all** - Apply all suggested improvements
- **critical** - Apply only critical issues
- **select** - I'll choose specific numbers
- **none** - Keep story as-is
- **details** - Show me more details about any suggestion

Your choice:
```

### **Step 7: Apply Selected Improvements**

When user accepts improvements:

- **Load the story file**
- **Apply accepted changes** (make them look natural, as if they were always there)
- **DO NOT reference** the review process, original LLM, or that changes were "added" or "enhanced"
- **Ensure clean, coherent final story** that reads as if it was created perfectly the first time

### **Step 8: Confirmation**

After applying changes:

```
✅ **STORY IMPROVEMENTS APPLIED**

Updated {{count}} sections in the story file.

The story now includes comprehensive developer guidance to prevent common implementation issues and ensure flawless execution.

**Next Steps:**
1. Review the updated story
2. Run `dev-story` for implementation
```

---

## **💪 COMPETITIVE EXCELLENCE MINDSET**

**Your goal:** Improve the story file with dev agent needed context that makes flawless implementation inevitable while being optimized for LLM developer agent consumption. Remember the dev agent will ONLY have this file to use.

**Success Criteria:** The LLM developer agent that processes your improved story will have:

- ✅ Clear technical requirements they must follow
- ✅ Previous work context they can build upon
- ✅ Anti-pattern prevention to avoid common mistakes
- ✅ Comprehensive guidance for efficient implementation
- ✅ **Optimized content structure** for maximum clarity and minimum token waste
- ✅ **Actionable instructions** with no ambiguity or verbosity
- ✅ **Efficient information density** - maximum guidance in minimum text

**Every improvement should make it IMPOSSIBLE for the developer to:**

- Reinvent existing solutions
- Use wrong approaches or libraries
- Create duplicate functionality
- Miss critical requirements
- Make implementation errors

**LLM Optimization Should Make it IMPOSSIBLE for the developer agent to:**

- Misinterpret requirements due to ambiguity
- Waste tokens on verbose, non-actionable content
- Struggle to find critical information buried in text
- Get confused by poor structure or organization
- Miss key implementation signals due to inefficient communication

**Go create the ultimate developer implementation guide! 🚀**

import logging
import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Header, HTTPException

from app.config.workflow_registry import workflow_registry
from app.core.exceptions import IntegrationError
from app.integrations.google_docs import GoogleDocsIntegration
from app.schemas.data import TaskItem, TasksResponse
from app.schemas.status import Meta

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/data", tags=["data"])

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_google_docs = GoogleDocsIntegration()


@router.get(
    "/tasks",
    response_model=TasksResponse,
    status_code=200,
)
async def get_tasks(
    x_autom9_session: str | None = Header(default=None),
) -> TasksResponse:
    """
    Fetch consultant task list from the configured Google Doc.

    Reads google_docs_url from the active workflow config's data_panel section.
    Returns 503 if integration is unavailable.
    Returns 404 if no data_panel config is present.
    No admin auth required — accessible to any session holder (same as /api/status).
    """
    active = workflow_registry.active_config
    if active is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No workflow config loaded")

    data_panel = active.get("data_panel")
    if not data_panel:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="data_panel not configured")

    google_docs_url = data_panel.get("google_docs_url")
    if not google_docs_url:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="google_docs_url not configured")

    logger.info(
        "data_tasks_fetch",
        extra={
            "session_id": x_autom9_session or "unknown",
            "integration": "google_docs",
        },
    )

    try:
        result = await _google_docs.execute("fetch_tasks", {"url": google_docs_url})
    except IntegrationError as exc:
        logger.warning(
            "data_tasks_fetch_failed",
            extra={"integration": exc.integration, "error": str(exc)},
        )
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc

    tasks = [TaskItem(text=str(item)) for item in result.get("tasks", [])]
    return TasksResponse(data=tasks, meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())))

# Dev Story Workflow

**Goal:** Execute story implementation following a context filled story spec file.

**Your Role:** Developer implementing the story.
- Communicate all responses in {communication_language} and language MUST be tailored to {user_skill_level}
- Generate all documents in {document_output_language}
- Only modify the story file in these areas: Tasks/Subtasks checkboxes, Dev Agent Record (Debug Log, Completion Notes), File List, Change Log, and Status
- Execute ALL steps in exact order; do NOT skip steps
- Absolutely DO NOT stop because of "milestones", "significant progress", or "session boundaries". Continue in a single execution until the story is COMPLETE (all ACs satisfied and all tasks/subtasks checked) UNLESS a HALT condition is triggered or the USER gives other instruction.
- Do NOT schedule a "next session" or request review pauses unless a HALT condition applies. Only Step 6 decides completion.
- User skill level ({user_skill_level}) affects conversation style ONLY, not code updates.

---

## INITIALIZATION

### Configuration Loading

Load config from `{project-root}/_bmad/bmm/config.yaml` and resolve:

- `project_name`, `user_name`
- `communication_language`, `document_output_language`
- `user_skill_level`
- `implementation_artifacts`
- `date` as system-generated current datetime

### Paths

- `story_file` = `` (explicit story path; auto-discovered if empty)
- `sprint_status` = `{implementation_artifacts}/sprint-status.yaml`

### Context

- `project_context` = `**/project-context.md` (load if exists)

---

## EXECUTION

<workflow>
  <critical>Communicate all responses in {communication_language} and language MUST be tailored to {user_skill_level}</critical>
  <critical>Generate all documents in {document_output_language}</critical>
  <critical>Only modify the story file in these areas: Tasks/Subtasks checkboxes, Dev Agent Record (Debug Log, Completion Notes), File List,
    Change Log, and Status</critical>
  <critical>Execute ALL steps in exact order; do NOT skip steps</critical>
  <critical>Absolutely DO NOT stop because of "milestones", "significant progress", or "session boundaries". Continue in a single execution
    until the story is COMPLETE (all ACs satisfied and all tasks/subtasks checked) UNLESS a HALT condition is triggered or the USER gives
    other instruction.</critical>
  <critical>Do NOT schedule a "next session" or request review pauses unless a HALT condition applies. Only Step 6 decides completion.</critical>
  <critical>User skill level ({user_skill_level}) affects conversation style ONLY, not code updates.</critical>

  <step n="1" goal="Find next ready story and load it" tag="sprint-status">
    <check if="{{story_path}} is provided">
      <action>Use {{story_path}} directly</action>
      <action>Read COMPLETE story file</action>
      <action>Extract story_key from filename or metadata</action>
      <goto anchor="task_check" />
    </check>

    <!-- Sprint-based story discovery -->
    <check if="{{sprint_status}} file exists">
      <critical>MUST read COMPLETE sprint-status.yaml file from start to end to preserve order</critical>
      <action>Load the FULL file: {{sprint_status}}</action>
      <action>Read ALL lines from beginning to end - do not skip any content</action>
      <action>Parse the development_status section completely to understand story order</action>

      <action>Find the FIRST story (by reading in order from top to bottom) where:
        - Key matches pattern: number-number-name (e.g., "1-2-user-auth")
        - NOT an epic key (epic-X) or retrospective (epic-X-retrospective)
        - Status value equals "ready-for-dev"
      </action>

      <check if="no ready-for-dev or in-progress story found">
        <output>📋 No ready-for-dev stories found in sprint-status.yaml

          **Current Sprint Status:** {{sprint_status_summary}}

          **What would you like to do?**
          1. Run `create-story` to create next story from epics with comprehensive context
          2. Run `*validate-create-story` to improve existing stories before development (recommended quality check)
          3. Specify a particular story file to develop (provide full path)
          4. Check {{sprint_status}} file to see current sprint status

          💡 **Tip:** Stories in `ready-for-dev` may not have been validated. Consider running `validate-create-story` first for a quality
          check.
        </output>
        <ask>Choose option [1], [2], [3], or [4], or specify story file path:</ask>

        <check if="user chooses '1'">
          <action>HALT - Run create-story to create next story</action>
        </check>

        <check if="user chooses '2'">
          <action>HALT - Run validate-create-story to improve existing stories</action>
        </check>

        <check if="user chooses '3'">
          <ask>Provide the story file path to develop:</ask>
          <action>Store user-provided story path as {{story_path}}</action>
          <goto anchor="task_check" />
        </check>

        <check if="user chooses '4'">
          <output>Loading {{sprint_status}} for detailed status review...</output>
          <action>Display detailed sprint status analysis</action>
          <action>HALT - User can review sprint status and provide story path</action>
        </check>

        <check if="user provides story file path">
          <action>Store user-provided story path as {{story_path}}</action>
          <goto anchor="task_check" />
        </check>
      </check>
    </check>

    <!-- Non-sprint story discovery -->
    <check if="{{sprint_status}} file does NOT exist">
      <action>Search {implementation_artifacts} for stories directly</action>
      <action>Find stories with "ready-for-dev" status in files</action>
      <action>Look for story files matching pattern: *-*-*.md</action>
      <action>Read each candidate story file to check Status section</action>

      <check if="no ready-for-dev stories found in story files">
        <output>📋 No ready-for-dev stories found

          **Available Options:**
          1. Run `create-story` to create next story from epics with comprehensive context
          2. Run `*validate-create-story` to improve existing stories
          3. Specify which story to develop
        </output>
        <ask>What would you like to do? Choose option [1], [2], or [3]:</ask>

        <check if="user chooses '1'">
          <action>HALT - Run create-story to create next story</action>
        </check>

        <check if="user chooses '2'">
          <action>HALT - Run validate-create-story to improve existing stories</action>
        </check>

        <check if="user chooses '3'">
          <ask>It's unclear what story you want developed. Please provide the full path to the story file:</ask>
          <action>Store user-provided story path as {{story_path}}</action>
          <action>Continue with provided story file</action>
        </check>
      </check>

      <check if="ready-for-dev story found in files">
        <action>Use discovered story file and extract story_key</action>
      </check>
    </check>

    <action>Store the found story_key (e.g., "1-2-user-authentication") for later status updates</action>
    <action>Find matching story file in {implementation_artifacts} using story_key pattern: {{story_key}}.md</action>
    <action>Read COMPLETE story file from discovered path</action>

    <anchor id="task_check" />

    <action>Parse sections: Story, Acceptance Criteria, Tasks/Subtasks, Dev Notes, Dev Agent Record, File List, Change Log, Status</action>

    <action>Load comprehensive context from story file's Dev Notes section</action>
    <action>Extract developer guidance from Dev Notes: architecture requirements, previous learnings, technical specifications</action>
    <action>Use enhanced story context to inform implementation decisions and approaches</action>

    <action>Identify first incomplete task (unchecked [ ]) in Tasks/Subtasks</action>

    <action if="no incomplete tasks">
      <goto step="6">Completion sequence</goto>
    </action>
    <action if="story file inaccessible">HALT: "Cannot develop story without access to story file"</action>
    <action if="incomplete task or subtask requirements ambiguous">ASK user to clarify or HALT</action>
  </step>

  <step n="2" goal="Load project context and story information">
    <critical>Load all available context to inform implementation</critical>

    <action>Load {project_context} for coding standards and project-wide patterns (if exists)</action>
    <action>Parse sections: Story, Acceptance Criteria, Tasks/Subtasks, Dev Notes, Dev Agent Record, File List, Change Log, Status</action>
    <action>Load comprehensive context from story file's Dev Notes section</action>
    <action>Extract developer guidance from Dev Notes: architecture requirements, previous learnings, technical specifications</action>
    <action>Use enhanced story context to inform implementation decisions and approaches</action>
    <output>✅ **Context Loaded**
      Story and project context available for implementation
    </output>
  </step>

  <step n="3" goal="Detect review continuation and extract review context">
    <critical>Determine if this is a fresh start or continuation after code review</critical>

    <action>Check if "Senior Developer Review (AI)" section exists in the story file</action>
    <action>Check if "Review Follow-ups (AI)" subsection exists under Tasks/Subtasks</action>

    <check if="Senior Developer Review section exists">
      <action>Set review_continuation = true</action>
      <action>Extract from "Senior Developer Review (AI)" section:
        - Review outcome (Approve/Changes Requested/Blocked)
        - Review date
        - Total action items with checkboxes (count checked vs unchecked)
        - Severity breakdown (High/Med/Low counts)
      </action>
      <action>Count unchecked [ ] review follow-up tasks in "Review Follow-ups (AI)" subsection</action>
      <action>Store list of unchecked review items as {{pending_review_items}}</action>

      <output>⏯️ **Resuming Story After Code Review** ({{review_date}})

        **Review Outcome:** {{review_outcome}}
        **Action Items:** {{unchecked_review_count}} remaining to address
        **Priorities:** {{high_count}} High, {{med_count}} Medium, {{low_count}} Low

        **Strategy:** Will prioritize review follow-up tasks (marked [AI-Review]) before continuing with regular tasks.
      </output>
    </check>

    <check if="Senior Developer Review section does NOT exist">
      <action>Set review_continuation = false</action>
      <action>Set {{pending_review_items}} = empty</action>

      <output>🚀 **Starting Fresh Implementation**

        Story: {{story_key}}
        Story Status: {{current_status}}
        First incomplete task: {{first_task_description}}
      </output>
    </check>
  </step>

  <step n="4" goal="Mark story in-progress" tag="sprint-status">
    <check if="{{sprint_status}} file exists">
      <action>Load the FULL file: {{sprint_status}}</action>
      <action>Read all development_status entries to find {{story_key}}</action>
      <action>Get current status value for development_status[{{story_key}}]</action>

      <check if="current status == 'ready-for-dev' OR review_continuation == true">
        <action>Update the story in the sprint status report to = "in-progress"</action>
        <action>Update last_updated field to current date</action>
        <output>🚀 Starting work on story {{story_key}}
          Status updated: ready-for-dev → in-progress
        </output>
      </check>

      <check if="current status == 'in-progress'">
        <output>⏯️ Resuming work on story {{story_key}}
          Story is already marked in-progress
        </output>
      </check>

      <check if="current status is neither ready-for-dev nor in-progress">
        <output>⚠️ Unexpected story status: {{current_status}}
          Expected ready-for-dev or in-progress. Continuing anyway...
        </output>
      </check>

      <action>Store {{current_sprint_status}} for later use</action>
    </check>

    <check if="{{sprint_status}} file does NOT exist">
      <output>ℹ️ No sprint status file exists - story progress will be tracked in story file only</output>
      <action>Set {{current_sprint_status}} = "no-sprint-tracking"</action>
    </check>
  </step>

  <step n="5" goal="Implement task following red-green-refactor cycle">
    <critical>FOLLOW THE STORY FILE TASKS/SUBTASKS SEQUENCE EXACTLY AS WRITTEN - NO DEVIATION</critical>

    <action>Review the current task/subtask from the story file - this is your authoritative implementation guide</action>
    <action>Plan implementation following red-green-refactor cycle</action>

import json
import logging
import time
import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Header, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.agent.masking import TokenMap, mask_text, rehydrate_text
from app.agent.provider_factory import get_provider
from app.config.workflow_registry import workflow_registry
from app.core.exceptions import ProviderError
from app.db.deps import get_db
from app.models.interaction_log import InteractionLog
from app.schemas.chat import ChatData, ChatRequest, ChatResponse
from app.schemas.status import Meta

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/chat", tags=["chat"])
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@router.post("", response_model=ChatResponse, status_code=200)
async def chat(
    body: ChatRequest,
    x_autom9_session: str | None = Header(default=None),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> ChatResponse:
    """
    Primary agent interaction endpoint.

    Applies masking pipeline on input before LLM call and rehydrates output
    before returning (FR17, FR18). Logs masked_input/masked_output only (NFR7).
    """
    active = workflow_registry.active_config
    if active is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No workflow config loaded")

    try:
        provider = await get_provider(db)
    except ProviderError as exc:
        logger.warning("chat_provider_unavailable", extra={"error": str(exc)})
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc

    tools = workflow_registry.get_tool_definitions()

    # Masking pipeline — TokenMap is per-request in v1.
    # Story 3.4 will register identifiable fields from session data before this call.
    token_map = TokenMap()
    masked_message = mask_text(body.message, token_map)

    # Build messages list: system → history → new user turn
    agent_instructions = active.get("agent_instructions", "")
    messages: list[dict] = []
    if agent_instructions:
        messages.append({"role": "system", "content": agent_instructions})
    for turn in body.history:
        messages.append({"role": turn.role, "content": turn.content})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": masked_message})

    start_ms = int(time.monotonic() * 1000)
    try:
        llm_response = await provider.complete(messages, tools)
    except ProviderError as exc:
        logger.warning("chat_llm_error", extra={"error": str(exc)})
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc
    latency_ms = int(time.monotonic() * 1000) - start_ms

    # masked_output is what LLM returned (it only ever saw masked inputs).
    # rehydrate before returning to consultant.
    masked_output = llm_response.content
    reply = rehydrate_text(masked_output, token_map)

    tool_calls_json = json.dumps(llm_response.tool_calls) if llm_response.tool_calls else None

    await _write_log(
        db=db,
        session_id_str=x_autom9_session,
        masked_input=masked_message,
        masked_output=masked_output,
        tool_calls=tool_calls_json,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
    )

    return ChatResponse(
        data=ChatData(reply=reply),
        meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())),
    )


async def _write_log(
    *,
    db: AsyncSession,
    session_id_str: str | None,
    masked_input: str,
    masked_output: str,
    tool_calls: str | None,
    latency_ms: int,
) -> None:
    """Write InteractionLog entry. Silently skips on any error (invalid session, FK miss)."""
    if not session_id_str:
        return
    try:
        session_id = uuid.UUID(session_id_str)
    except ValueError:
        logger.warning("chat_invalid_session_header", extra={"header": session_id_str})
        return
    try:
        log_entry = InteractionLog(
            session_id=session_id,
            masked_input=masked_input,
            masked_output=masked_output,
            tool_calls=tool_calls,
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
        )
        db.add(log_entry)
        await db.flush()
        logger.info(
            "chat_turn_logged",
            extra={"session_id": str(session_id), "latency_ms": latency_ms},
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("chat_log_write_failed", extra={"error": str(exc)})

import pytest
from httpx import AsyncClient
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

from app.agent.provider import LLMResponse

pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope="session")

SESSION_HEADERS = {"X-Autom9-Session": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"}

_BASE_CONFIG = {
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "workflow_id": "planning",
    "tools": [],
    "agent_instructions": "You are a planning assistant.",
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No active config → 404
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def test_chat_no_config_returns_404(client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch):
    import app.api.chat as chat_module
    from app.config.workflow_registry import WorkflowRegistry

    registry = WorkflowRegistry()
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "workflow_registry", registry)

    response = await client.post("/api/chat", json={"message": "hello"}, headers=SESSION_HEADERS)
    assert response.status_code == 404


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provider not configured → 503
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def test_chat_no_provider_returns_503(client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch):
    import app.api.chat as chat_module
    from app.config.workflow_registry import WorkflowRegistry
    from app.core.exceptions import ProviderError

    registry = WorkflowRegistry()
    registry._active = _BASE_CONFIG
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "workflow_registry", registry)

    async def _fail_provider(db):
        raise ProviderError("none", "No active LLM provider configured.")

    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "get_provider", _fail_provider)

    response = await client.post("/api/chat", json={"message": "hello"}, headers=SESSION_HEADERS)
    assert response.status_code == 503
    body = response.json()
    assert body["error"]["code"] == "PROVIDER_ERROR"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LLM call raises ProviderError → 503
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def test_chat_llm_error_returns_503(client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch):
    import app.api.chat as chat_module
    from app.config.workflow_registry import WorkflowRegistry
    from app.core.exceptions import ProviderError

    registry = WorkflowRegistry()
    registry._active = _BASE_CONFIG
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "workflow_registry", registry)

    mock_provider = AsyncMock()
    mock_provider.complete.side_effect = ProviderError("openai", "Rate limit exceeded")
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "get_provider", AsyncMock(return_value=mock_provider))

    response = await client.post("/api/chat", json={"message": "hello"}, headers=SESSION_HEADERS)
    assert response.status_code == 503


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happy path — returns reply
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def test_chat_returns_reply(client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch):
    import app.api.chat as chat_module
    from app.config.workflow_registry import WorkflowRegistry

    registry = WorkflowRegistry()
    registry._active = _BASE_CONFIG
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "workflow_registry", registry)

    mock_provider = AsyncMock()
    mock_provider.complete.return_value = LLMResponse(
        content="I can help with that.",
        tool_calls=[],
        finish_reason="stop",
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "get_provider", AsyncMock(return_value=mock_provider))

    response = await client.post(
        "/api/chat",
        json={"message": "What are my open days?"},
        headers=SESSION_HEADERS,
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body["data"]["reply"] == "I can help with that."
    assert "request_id" in body["meta"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Multi-turn — history included in LLM call
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def test_chat_history_included_in_llm_call(client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch):
    import app.api.chat as chat_module
    from app.config.workflow_registry import WorkflowRegistry

    registry = WorkflowRegistry()
    registry._active = _BASE_CONFIG
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "workflow_registry", registry)

    captured: dict = {}

    async def _capture_complete(messages, tools):
        captured["messages"] = messages
        return LLMResponse(content="Got it.", tool_calls=[], finish_reason="stop")

    mock_provider = AsyncMock()
    mock_provider.complete.side_effect = _capture_complete
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "get_provider", AsyncMock(return_value=mock_provider))

    response = await client.post(
        "/api/chat",
        json={
            "message": "Follow-up question",
            "history": [
                {"role": "user", "content": "First message"},
                {"role": "assistant", "content": "First reply"},
            ],
        },
        headers=SESSION_HEADERS,
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200

    msgs = captured["messages"]
    # system + 2 history turns + new user turn = 4
    assert len(msgs) == 4
    assert msgs[0]["role"] == "system"
    assert msgs[1]["content"] == "First message"
    assert msgs[2]["content"] == "First reply"
    assert msgs[3]["content"] == "Follow-up question"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No session header — chat still works, logging skipped
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def test_chat_no_session_header_still_succeeds(client: AsyncClient, monkeypatch):
    import app.api.chat as chat_module
    from app.config.workflow_registry import WorkflowRegistry

    registry = WorkflowRegistry()
    registry._active = _BASE_CONFIG
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "workflow_registry", registry)

    mock_provider = AsyncMock()
    mock_provider.complete.return_value = LLMResponse(
        content="Hello!", tool_calls=[], finish_reason="stop"
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(chat_module, "get_provider", AsyncMock(return_value=mock_provider))

    response = await client.post("/api/chat", json={"message": "Hi"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["data"]["reply"] == "Hello!"
